reforms.description: The Canadian government introduced a new system of outright grants to replace the previous tax concessions for scientific research expenditures, which were aimed at increasing research outlays by firms.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Providing outright grants encourages firms to invest more in research, which can lead to innovation and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The new system has been put into practice and is operational.
reforms.importance_rationale: The introduction of a new funding system is significant but not a major overhaul of the funding landscape.
reforms.source_quote: The tax concessions previously in force regarding expenditures on scientific research... are to be replaced by a system of outright grants.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The reform introduces a new system of outright grants to replace tax concessions for scientific research expenditures, aimed at increasing research outlays by firms.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The Canadian government has expanded its technical and vocational training programs, significantly increasing participation among the labor force to enhance skills and employability.
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Enhancing skills and employability contributes to a more skilled workforce, which supports productivity and innovation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The program has been expanded and is currently operational.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: The expansion of training programs is significant but not a structural overhaul.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The programme of technical and vocational training has been considerably expanded; in 1964, almost 1 per cent of the labour force participated in training programmes.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on expanding technical and vocational training programs, which does not directly relate to R&D funding or knowledge transfer.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Canada replaced its tax concession system for scientific research expenditures with a system of outright grants. Previously, firms could claim current research outlays as a business expense plus an additional 50% of the extent to which these exceeded 1961 research expenditures. The new grant system is expected to lead to further increases in research outlays.
all_reforms_including_excluded.package_name: 1965 Industrial Efficiency and Technological Standards Programme
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Replacing tax concessions with direct grants removes administrative complexity and is expected to stimulate private-sector R&D investment, raising innovation capacity and productivity.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: The text states: 'The tax concessions previously in force regarding expenditures on scientific research... are to be replaced by a system of outright grants.'
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: A significant shift in the design of R&D support instruments from indirect (tax concessions) to direct (grants), expected to increase research outlays. Narrower in scope than a system-wide overhaul but meaningful for private-sector innovation incentives.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: The tax concessions previously in force regarding expenditures on scientific research, under which a firm could claim not only its current research outlays as a business expense but also an additional 50 per cent of the extent to which these exceeded its research expenditures in 1961, are to be replaced by a system of outright grants.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: This reform is similar to 'ac_0' but is only supported by one model; it does not provide additional clarity or new information to warrant inclusion.
